To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
CsrA inhibits ribosome binding to the cstA ShineDalgarno sequence by binding to three or four sites in the cstA transcript, two of which overlap the Shine-Dalgarnoto sequence.
CsrA blocks ribosome binding to the cstA transcript and regulates cstA expression by binding to four sites in its RNA.
CsrA inhibits translation of the Eschericia coli carbon starvation gene, cstA, in vitro by binding directly to the cstA transcript and blocking ribosome binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new genes regulated by Csr, and we have shown that the CstA peptide transport protein is regulated by Csr.
the identification, characterization, and regulation of genes that are regulated by Csr.
the regulation of the cstA gene in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CsrA regulation of cstA is a novel mechanism for controlling translation of a gene encoding a peptide transporter.
CsrA inhibits the expression of cstA by blocking ribosome binding to the cstA transcript.

CsrA inhibits translation of the Eschericia coli carbon starvation gene, cstA, in a manner that is dependent on the Shine-DalgarnO sequence and that is independent of the cAMP-cAMP receptor protein complex or the σS factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CsrA blocks ribosome access to transcripts that contain a CsrA binding sequence in their leader regions.
CsrA inhibits translation by interfering with ribosome access to transcripts.
CsrA blocks ribosome access to transcripts that contain CsrA binding motifs in the Shine-DalgarnO region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CsrA can regulate translation initiation at a second site in addition to the glgCAP site.
CsrA can block translation by binding to a site that overlaps the ribosome binding site.
CsrA can regulate the expression of genes by blocking ribosome access.
